subject: Copywriting
title: Email vs. Social Media ROI
description: A micro-lesson that makes Email vs. Social Media ROI usable.

hook.text: Email generates $36 for every $1 spent. Social media generates $2.80. Email outperforms social by 12x.

buildup.text: Social platforms control reach. Facebook shows your post to 5% of followers. Email reaches 85-90% of inboxes.

discovery.text: Email converts 3x better than social media for purchases. The private inbox creates focused, undistracted reading.

twist.text: Despite the data, most brands spend 10x more on social than email. Marketing budgets follow trends, not ROI.

climax.text: Smart marketers use social to grow the email list, then email to drive revenue. The funnel ends in the inbox.

punchline.text: $36 return per $1 spent. Email is the ROI king.

quiz.question: What is the average ROI of email marketing?

details.summary: Email marketing consistently delivers higher return on investment than any social media platform. Studies show email generates roughly $36 for every $1 spent, while social media typically returns $2-5. The difference lies in ownership: email lists are owned assets, while social followers are...
details.whyItMatters: Marketers who over-invest in social media at the expense of email leave money on the table. Understanding the ROI gap helps allocate budgets where they produce the most revenue.
takeaways: Email ROI averages $36 per $1 spent versus $2-5 for social media
Email lists are owned assets not subject to algorithm changes
Social platforms can restrict reach at any time without notice

faq.question: Why does email outperform social media in ROI?
faq.answer: Email reaches subscribers directly without algorithmic filtering. When you send an email, 90%+ reach the inbox. Social posts typically reach 1-5% of followers organically. Email also reaches people who have explicitly opted in, making them more receptive to offers.

faq.question: Should brands abandon social media for email?
faq.answer: No — social media excels at brand awareness and community building. The best strategy uses social to attract audiences and email to convert and retain them. Social media builds the top of the funnel; email drives the bottom.
